newsitem.title: USA: Riser Foods expense recognition hurt Q2 EPS.
newsitem.headline: Riser Foods expense recognition hurt Q2 EPS.

text.p: Riser Foods Inc, reporting higher fiscal second quarter sales and earnings, said Tuesday its results were hurt by the timing of expense recognized in connection with its annual incentive program.
Had the expense been recognized under its annual incentive program between years, net income per share for the second quarter would have been $0.11 higher, it said.
The company said it does not anticipate any significant additional expense to be recognized under its annual incentive program for the remainder of fiscal 1997.
It said net income for the second quarter rose to $5.0 million, or $.62 per share, from $4.6 million, or $.56 per share, a year earlier.
It was the highest quarterly income in Riser's nine-year history, it said.
Net sales increased to a second-quarter record $321.8 million from $301.7 million a year earlier.
"We are pleased with the continued strength of our operating results," said Anthony Rego, chairman and chief executive officer.
"Initiatives designed to position Riser for long-term, profitable growth have proven successful and continue to drive our results," he said.
He added, "The strength of our financial results allows us the flexibility to continue to look for strategic acquisitions that will grow our operations further."
